record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every tetracyclic graph G on n vertices with n at least 26, is the energy of G at most the energy of P_n^{6,6;6,6}, with equality only for P_n^{6,6;6,6}? Here P_n^{6,6;6,6} denotes the graph obtained from four copies of C6 and a path P(n−24) by adding a single edge from two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the other two 6-cycles to the other endpoint.

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the quadricyclic (also called tetracyclic) graphs maximizing the energy remains open... For n ≥ 26, we have a general conjecture obtained with AutoGraphiX. First, let P_n^{6,6;6,6} denote the graph on n ≥ 26 obtained from four copies of C_6 and a path P_{n-24} by adding a single edge between each of two copies of C_6 to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from each of the two other copies of C_6 to the other endpoint of the P_{n-24}. Conjecture 5.12... Let G be a tetracyclic graph on n vertices with n ≥ 26. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6,6;6,6}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The energy of a finite simple graph $G$ is defined as $E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\lambda_i|$, where $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ are the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$. A connected graph on $n$ vertices is called tetracyclic (or quadricyclic) if it has exactly $n+3$ edges (equivalently, cyclomatic number $4$).

For each integer $n\ge 26$, define the graph $P_n^{6,6;6,6}$ as follows. Take four vertex-disjoint copies $C^{(1)},C^{(2)},C^{(3)},C^{(4)}$ of the cycle $C_6$ and a vertex-disjoint path $P_{n-24}$ on $n-24$ vertices with endpoints $u$ and $v$. Choose one vertex $x_i$ in each $C^{(i)}$. Add the edges $x_1u$, $x_2u$, $x_3v$, $x_4v$. The resulting graph has $n$ vertices and $4\cdot 6 + (n-25) + 4 = n+3$ edges, hence is tetracyclic.

Prove or disprove: for every tetracyclic graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $n\ge 26$,
$$E(G)\le E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}),$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong P_n^{6,6;6,6}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface surveys and papers on extremal-energy problems for unicyclic, bicyclic, tricyclic, and tetracyclic graphs. The unicyclic case has been fully resolved and the tricyclic analogue (with $P_n^{6,6,6}$) is partially known but still open in general; no source located indicates that the tetracyclic conjecture identifying $P_n^{6,6;6,6}$ as the unique maximum-energy tetracyclic graph for $n\ge 26$ has been proved or disproved. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Graphs Extremal with Regard to Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing extremal energy results for trees, unicyclic, bicyclic, tricyclic and tetracyclic graphs, with several conjectures still open.
status_evidence.claim: Tetracyclic maximum-energy conjecture is listed among open extremal-energy problems.

status_evidence.title: Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the unicyclic analogue, while higher-cyclomatic analogues are noted as remaining.
status_evidence.claim: The unicyclic case is fully solved; tricyclic/tetracyclic analogues remain.

status_evidence.title: On a Conjecture about Tricyclic Graphs with Maximal Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the tricyclic analogue $P_n^{6,6,6}$; tetracyclic case not addressed there.
status_evidence.claim: Tricyclic conjecture is the closest related result, and tetracyclic case is not resolved in this line of work.
